# Results -- Study 508 (Momentum-Crashes) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: the canonical
Jegadeesh-Titman 12-1 cross-sectional momentum book (rank by trailing 12-month return skipping
the most recent month, long the top quintile / short the bottom, equal-weight, dollar-neutral,
monthly hold, one execution lag), then its **crash anatomy**, **Daniel-Moskowitz regime
conditioning**, and the **vol-scaling repair**, on a large-cap S&P 500 survivor basket.
As-of **2026-06-26**. Fingerprint `e76dff230f36`.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3424 days x 38 tickers | `e038fa42cc02` |
| SPY (market proxy, regimes) | 4023 days | `35681d7ebf6e` |
| Period covered | 2012-05-18 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |
| WML holding months | 151 (2013-05 -- 2025-11) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True), **price-only** (the WML
spread is self-financing and dollar-neutral; no separate risk-free leg). Basket: 38 large-cap
names with >= 80% coverage. SPY is used only for the bear/panic regime indicators.

**Survivorship bias (named on the SIGNAL axis):** the basket is names *still trading in 2026*,
projected backwards. The loser leg's natural short candidates -- firms that trended down into
delisting/bankruptcy -- are absent. This **inflates the WML premium** (upper bound) AND
**understates the crash** (the worst loser-leg snap-backs were the delisted names we never see).
Opt-in guard: pass a delisting-complete panel to `long_short` to lift the bias.

## The signal -- 12-1 winners-minus-losers (quintile, dollar-neutral)

One execution lag: the 12-1 signal is formed on the month-end close; we enter the next month and
earn its realised return. No same-bar fill, no look-ahead.

| Statistic | Gross | Net (10bps/leg + 50bps borrow) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean return (annualised) | **-0.34%/yr** | **-1.43%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 16.10%/yr | -- |
| Sharpe | -0.021 | -- |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.072** | -- |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 54.3% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -44.9% | -- |
| Worst month | -17.7% | -- |
| Skewness | **-0.63** | -- |
| Avg turnover | 24.8%/mo | -- |

- The WML spread earns **-0.34%/yr gross** at HAC *t* = **-0.072** -- statistically
  indistinguishable from zero. After 10bps/leg + 50bps/yr borrow it is **-1.43%/yr net**.
- **Label-shuffle placebo** (2000 permutations): real mean -0.34%/yr vs placebo mean -0.07%/yr,
  one-sided **p = 0.537**. The signal does not beat a coin.
- The **negative skew (-0.63)** is the crash signature: even with a flat mean, the distribution
  is left-tailed -- the strategy gives back its small wins in a few violent months.

## The crash anatomy

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Deepest drawdown | **-44.9%** (peak 2020-09-30 -> trough 2025-10-31) |
| Worst month | **2020-10-31: -17.7%** (winners +8.1%, **losers +25.8%**) |
| 2nd worst | 2025-07-31: -14.0% (winners -0.7%, losers +13.2%) |
| 3rd worst | 2022-12-31: -13.5% (winners +0.4%, losers +13.9%) |
| 4th worst | 2021-01-31: -12.6% (winners -0.8%, losers +11.8%) |

Every crash month is driven by the **short (loser) leg snapping back**, not the long leg
falling -- exactly the Daniel-Moskowitz (2016) mechanism. October 2020 is the textbook case: in
the vaccine-news rebound the beaten-down value/cyclical names (the shorts) ripped +25.8% in one
month while the winners managed only +8.1%, costing the dollar-neutral book -17.7%.

## Daniel-Moskowitz regime conditioning

Bear indicator = trailing 12-month SPY return < 0; "down" = SPY down this month; "panic" = bear
**and** the market is rebounding this month. (A 24-month bear window almost never fires on a
large-cap survivor tape that recovers fast -- see notebook 02 for the sweep.)

| Regime | WML mean (annualised) | Months |
|---|--:|--:|
| All | -0.34%/yr | 151 |
| Calm (non-bear) | +0.67%/yr | 134 |
| Bear (any) | **-8.25%/yr** | 17 |
| Bear & down | **-27.82%/yr** | 10 |
| Panic (bear & rebound) | +19.71%/yr | 7 |

Momentum's return is **regime-dependent**: flat-to-positive in calm markets (+0.67%/yr) but
bleeding **-8.25%/yr in bear markets** and **-27.82%/yr in bear-and-down months**. The
panic/rebound cell is thin (7 months) and noisy here -- on this survivor basket the violent
loser snap-backs land in the worst-month table above rather than averaging cleanly into the
panic cell.

## The repair -- vol-scaled (dynamic) momentum

Constant-volatility momentum: scale the WML position inversely to the trailing 6-month realised
vol of the spread (known at *t*, no look-ahead), targeting 12%/yr ex-ante vol, leverage cap 3x.

| Statistic | Gross WML | Vol-scaled |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean (annualised) | -0.34%/yr | **+2.21%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 16.10%/yr | 15.99%/yr |
| Sharpe | -0.021 | **+0.138** |
| HAC t-stat | -0.072 | +0.492 |
| Max drawdown | -44.9% | **-35.6%** |
| Worst month | -17.7% | -15.9% |
| Skewness | **-0.63** | **-0.27** |

Vol-scaling **demonstrably tames the left tail**: skewness halves (-0.63 -> -0.27), the deepest
drawdown shrinks by ~9pts (-44.9% -> -35.6%), and the Sharpe flips from slightly negative to
slightly positive. It does *not* manufacture a tradable edge (t = +0.49, still < 2) -- it
repairs the *shape* of the return, not the *level*. This is the Daniel-Moskowitz result faithfully
reproduced: dynamic momentum is a better-behaved version of the same flat premium.

| 0.15 | +19.77%/yr | +4.64 | 107 |
| 0.30 | +45.54%/yr | +9.80 | 107 |
| 0.50 | +84.76%/yr | +13.96 | 107 |

The engine recovers a planted relative-strength drift monotonically and clears the bar when the
effect is real -- so the flat real-tape verdict reflects **the market**, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** WML -0.34%/yr, HAC *t* = -0.072, placebo *p* = 0.537. The most replicated
  anomaly in finance earns nothing on a 38-name large-cap survivor basket -- and survivorship
  already biases this *upward*. Literature support (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993, Daniel-Moskowitz 2016)
  does not lift a real-tape stamp; the tape is flat.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Net -1.43%/yr after costs, -44.9% drawdown, -0.63 skew. There is no
  positive expectancy to monetise and a fat crash risk to carry.
- **Does the crash exist, and does vol-scaling repair it? -- CONFIRMED.** The crash is real and
  loser-leg-driven (worst month -17.7%, all from shorts ripping +25.8%; momentum bleeds
  -27.8%/yr in bear-and-down months). Vol-scaling halves the negative skew (-0.63 -> -0.27) and
  shaves 9pts off the deepest drawdown (-44.9% -> -35.6%) -- exactly the Daniel-Moskowitz repair,
  fixing the *shape* without conjuring a tradable *level*.
